devasthanName: Shri Kshetra Macchindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir
aboutTempleContent1: Shri Kshetra Macchindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir is a revered temple located in Sawaragaon, Ashti, in the Beed district of Maharashtra. The temple is dedicated to Lord Macchindranath, a revered saint and spiritual figure. The temple is known for its serene atmosphere and spiritual significance, attracting devotees from all over the region. It serves as a place of worship, meditation, and community gatherings, fostering a sense of devotion and spirituality among its visitors.
aboutTempleContent2: The saga of Lord Machhindranath (also known as Matsyendranath) begins in the primordial era. According to the sacred Puranas, while Lord Shiva (Adinath) was revealing the secret of Brahmavidya and Yoga to Goddess Parvati on the banks of the cosmic ocean, a fish in the water listened with absolute stillness and devotion. Upon realizing the fish had attained divine enlightenment, Lord Shiva transformed it into a celestial mahayogi. Thus, he was named Machhindranath—the first human Guru of the Nath Sampradaya, born directly from the grace of Mahadev.

paushyaAmavasyaText: Paushya Amavasya marks the sacred day when Lord Macchindranath took Sanjivan Samadhi, entering eternal meditation at His holy resting place. On this auspicious occasion, a grand Chhabina procession and traditional Hanganma celebrations are held, as devotees gather with deep devotion to offer prayers and seek divine blessings at the Samadhi Sthal. The temple is beautifully decorated, and special rituals are performed to commemorate this auspicious occasion.
falgunAmavasyaText: On this sacred day, the holy Samadhi of Lord Macchindranath is opened once a year. At 1:00 PM, it is bathed with Ganga and other sacred waters, and at 4:00 PM, lakhs of devotees offer fragrant masala and chandan lep before it is respectfully covered before sunrise on Gudi Padwa.
rangPanchamiText: On the auspicious days of Chaturthi, Rang Panchami, and Nath Shashti, lakhs of devotees from Maharashtra and across the state gather with “Manache Nishan,” arriving with great devotion and celebration to seek the divine darshan of Shri Machchindranath’s sacred Samadhi, reflecting the centuries-old cultural heritage of Nath Sampradaya.
rushiPanchamiText: Rushi Panchami celebrates the divine birth of Lord Macchindranath, the great yogi and spiritual guide. On this auspicious day, devotees offer prayers, bhajans, and heartfelt devotion in honor of His sacred incarnation.
monthlyAmavasyaText: On the day of Amavasya, devotees gather at the temple to offer their prayers and seek blessings. The temple is beautifully decorated, and special rituals are performed to commemorate this auspicious occasion. Devotees participate in various religious activities, including offering flowers, lighting lamps, and performing puja to honor Lord Macchindranath and seek his divine blessings.

aboutMandirTitle: A Sacred Sanjivani Samadhi Temple of the Nath
aboutMandirText1: Nestled on the sacred hill of Machindranath Gad at Mayamba (Sawargaon), Maharashtra, the revered Machindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir stands as one of the most spiritually powerful centers of the Nath Sampradaya.
aboutMandirText2: This holy shrine marks the sacred place where Machindranath consciously entered Sanjivani Samadhi — voluntarily leaving his earthly body while in deep yogic meditation.
aboutMandirText3: For centuries, this divine Samadhi Sthal has radiated intense spiritual vibrations, drawing lakhs of devotees from across Maharashtra and neighboring regions. It is not merely a temple — it is a living spiritual legacy of the Nath tradition.
aboutMandirText4: From the sacred Machindranath Gad of Sawargaon to the broader Nath spiritual geography, the divine presence of Shri Machindranath Maharaj continues to inspire millions. Machindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir is not just a place of worship —It is a center of meditation, faith, fulfillment, and divine consciousness.
aboutMandirText6: A pillar of the Nath Sampradaya
aboutMachindranathGadText1: The hill shrine, fondly known as Machindranath Gad, is regarded as:
aboutMachindranathGadText3: A center of high spiritual energy
aboutMachindranathGadText4: A sacred pilgrimage site for Nath and Warkari followers
aboutMachindranathGadText5: A powerful seat of Sanjivani Samadhi
aboutMachindranathGadText6: Although Shri Machindranath Maharaj traveled across Nepal, Tibet, and South India spreading spiritual wisdom, Sawargaon holds supreme spiritual importance in Maharashtra, for it is here that he chose eternal meditation.
aboutMachindranathGadText7: Lakhs of devotees testify to experiencing peace, fulfillment of vows, mental balance, and divine grace upon visiting this sacred place.
symbolOfFaithText1: For generations, devotees have believed that sincere prayers offered at the Sanjivani Samadhi bring: Fulfillment of wishes, Protection from obstacles, Mental peace, Divine guidance, Spiritual awakening
symbolOfFaithText2: The temple continues to be a place where faith meets experience and devotion transforms into inner peace.
templeRenovationText1: To further enhance the spiritual brilliance of Mayamba Devasthan, an ambitious and historic renovation project has been undertaken by the Temple Trust.
templeRenovationText2: A grand and divine temple structure is being built:
templeRenovationText4: Construction Material: Premium black stone from Nanded,Maharashtra.
templeRenovationText8: Each pillar carved with sculptures of the 64 Yoginis.
templeRenovationText10: Designed to last for thousands of years.
templeRenovationText11: Keeping in mind the growing number of Nath devotees in the coming generations, the Trust has resolved to build a temple that reflects the spiritual greatness of the Nath Sampradaya.
templeRenovationText12: The goal is to complete this sacred project within the next three years through devotee contributions.
templeRenovationText13: The Trust Chairman Dadasaheb Chitale and Secretary Babasaheb Mhaske have appealed to devotees to contribute according to their devotion and faith.”
templeRenovationText14: This temple will stand not only as a magnificent architectural structure but as: A preservation of Nath spiritual heritage, A beacon of Sanjivani tradition, A sacred landmark for future generations
visionText: To establish the sacred Sanjivani Samadhi Sthal as a globally recognized spiritual center of the Nath tradition, preserving its divine legacy for generations to come.
mission1: Preserve Nath teachings and sacred rituals.
mission4: Serve pilgrims with dedication and facilities.
mission5: Promote spiritual awakening and social harmony.
promisText1: The Machindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir Trust is committed to:
promisText3: Serving devotees with transparency and devotion
promisText5: Completing the grand temple for generations to come
socialInitativeText: At Machindranath Sanjivani Samadhi Mandir, devotion is expressed not only through prayer but through selfless service (Seva). Guided by the spiritual teachings of Machindranath, the Temple Trust remains committed to serving society with compassion, responsibility, and dedication.
goshala: Sacred Goshala – Protection of Gau Mata :
goshalaText1: The temple lovingly operates a Goshala (cow sanctuary) that houses and cares for nearly 200 cows and their calves.The Goshala is dedicated to:
goshalaText2: Protection and preservation of indigenous cows, Providing shelter, nutritious food, and medical care, Maintaining a clean and sacred environment, Upholding the traditional dharmic value of Gau Seva
goshalaText3: Cows hold deep spiritual significance in Indian culture, and the temple considers their service an essential part of its spiritual responsibility.
annadanText1: In keeping with the sacred tradition of Annadan (offering food as charity), the temple conducts free community meals every day.
annadanText2: Annadan is offered every afternoon, Prasad is distributed again in the evening after Aarti.
annadanText3: Hundreds of devotees and visitors receive blessed meals daily, irrespective of caste, background, or status. The temple believes that Annadan is the greatest donation, as it nourishes both body and soul.
ambulanceText1: Understanding the needs of the surrounding rural region, the Temple Trust also operates a free ambulance service for emergency situations.
ambulanceText2: Assists devotees and local villagers during medical emergencies, Ensures timely transportation to hospitals, Reflects the temple’s commitment to humanitarian service.
ambulanceText3: The ambulance service stands as a symbol of compassionate outreach, extending spiritual care into practical service.
